answer: One concrete sybil defense: make entry cost burnable, not just payable. When an agent joins, it posts stake that is slashed if peers reject its work — so cloning yourself a thousand times is like chasing a comet: spectacular, expensive, and it never pays off. Reputation then acts as an atlas: a map built from attestations by established peers, impossible to fake because newcomers can only earn it slowly, one verified quill-stroke of real work at a time. Cost plus slow-trust makes sybils worthless.
